To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the genetic value of the analysed dairy and conformation characteristics of Polish Black-and-White Holstein-Friesians increased in the analysed period.

the genetic value of the conformation traits in Polish Black-and-White Holstein-Friesia cows is positively correlated with the genetic value for dairy production, while the genetic value for conformation traits in young cows is positively correlated to the genetic value of their parents.
the dairy traits and conformation traits are positively correlated, which means that cows that are good for milk yield are also good for conformation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a genetic analysis of the conformation traits of Holstein-Friesians in Poland, which is an essential element for the development of breeding programmes in dairy cows.

the estimation of the genetic value and trends of conformation traits of Polish Black-and-White Holstein cows, as well as with the analysis of the relations between the genetic value of the conformation and the dairy traits.
the analysis of the relations of the conformation traits of Holstein-Friesians with dairy performance and the genetic values of the traits analysed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the dairy production level and the year of birth of the animal do not have a statistically significant impact on the genetic value of the conformation traits analysed, while the genetic value of udder and temperament traits depends on the production level of the animal.
the genetic value of the conformation traits in the cows analysed is higher in cows with the highest genetic value of dairy production and in cows born in the most recent years.
the genetic value of the conformation traits in Polish Holsteins is high, but the level of genetic improvement is low.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results obtained confirm the usefulness of using the conformation traits in breeding programmes.
the conformation traits are genetically positively correlated with dairy traits, but their genetic value is low and does not exceed 0.3.

the highest genetic value of the analysed traits was obtained for the cows of the highest dairy production genetic value, and that in the group of cows with the highest dairy production values the genetic value of all traits analysed was the highest.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genetic values of dairy and conformational traits are positively correlated, which means that cows of high genetic value for dairy traits are also characterized by good conformational traits.

the genetic value of the conformation traits of the Polish Holstein-Freesian cows is increasing and the genetic value of these traits is positively correlated with the genetic value for the dairy production traits.
the conformation traits of dairy cows should be analysed taking into account their genetic value of dairy production, which is the most important factor in the selection of dairy cows.
